answer: In an opal trading network, the settlement kernel requires each voting agent to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before its vote counts. An attacker can mirror an agent’s software and invent thousands of names, but each voting identity needs a separate bond; the same tokens cannot back two identities at once. Creating 1,000 eligible identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing a capital requirement and lost investment income.
